subject: question about differences in variance obtained from Cameletti and Blangiardo example code

messages.author: 778bd0cef6c473fc
messages.subject: question about differences in variance obtained from Cameletti and Blangiardo example code
parts:
Hello,

I have two very basic statistics questions that I think this group can help with. My model is a standard convolution model (BYM or besag + iid), e.g.,


mod = inla(y ~ x1 + x2 + f(blockID, model = ‘bym’, graph.file = adjGraph), family= ‘binomial’, data=data)


I took the following code from Cameletti et al. 2012, p. 18-19. Cameletti et al. use this code to calculate the ‘mean and quantiles associated with variance of the Gaussian observation.’

sigma2eps_marg = inla.tmarginal(function(x) 1/x, mod$marginals.hyperpar$"Precision for the Gaussian observations")

….

I used Cameletti's code to obtain the mean and quantiles associated with the spatially structured and uncorrelated (‘iid’) random effects. See below.

#calculate mean, quantiles of uncorrelated (iid) variance

sigma2eps_marg = inla.tmarginal(function(x) 1/x, mod$marginals.hyperpar$"Precision for blockID (spatial component)")

sigma2eps_m1 = inla.emarginal(function(x) x, sigma2eps_marg)

sigma2eps_m2 = inla.emarginal(function(x) x^2, sigma2eps_marg)

sigma2eps_stdev = sqrt(sigma2eps_m2 - sigma2eps_m1^2)

sigma2eps_quantiles = inla.qmarginal(c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), sigma2eps_marg)

 

print(c(mean=sigma2eps_m1, sd=sigma2eps_stdev , "0.025quant" = sigma2eps_quantiles[1], "0.975quant" = sigma2eps_quantiles[3]))

 

I use the same code to calculate the mean and quantiles of uncorrelated (iid) variance (everything the same as above except for first line of code). 

 

However, I also found this code in Blangiardo et al. 2012 (London suicides example). Blangiardo et al use this code to obtain an estimate of the variance for the structured and uncorrelated terms, but the values are not the same as those I obtain using the previous code (Cameletti’s code). Also, it seems that obtaining the variance is done differently in these two pieces of example code: 

mat.marg<-matrix(NA, nrow=Nareas, ncol=1000)
m<-mod$marginals.random$ID
for (i in 1:Nareas){
  u<-m[[Nareas+i]]
  s<-inla.rmarginal(1000, u)
  mat.marg[i,]<-s}
var.RRspatial<-mean(apply(mat.marg, 2, sd))^2
var.RRhet<-inla.emarginal(function(x) 1/x, mod$marginals.hyper$"Precision for blockID (iid component)")
 
var.RRspatial/(var.RRspatial+var.RRhet)

 

Here are my questions:

1.       1. Is it correct to use Cameletti’s code to calculate the mean and quantiles (0.025, 0.975) for the spatially structured anduncorrelated  variances?


2.       2. If it is correct to use Cameletti’s code, why are the numbers I get from Blangiardo and Cameletti’s code different? The variance (Blangiardo’s var.RRhet and var.RRspatial) are not equal to the sigma2eps_m1 for spatial oriid variances, which I don’t understand. If the output of Cameletti vs. Blangiardo’s code are in fact different and are supposed to be different, can you just briefly explain what is the difference between these two approaches to obtaining and reporting the variance? And if they are supposed to be the same, why aren't they?


I know these are probably very simple questions, statistically speaking: thank you SO much for your help. I really appreciate your time.

Mercedes

> patial+var.RRhet)

>  
> Here are my questions:
> 1.       1. Is it correct to use Cameletti’s code to calculate the
> mean and quantiles (0.025, 0.975) for the spatially structured
> anduncorrelated  variances?

the B&C code is done using sampling because they wanted the posterior
for the relative variance, 

var.1/(var.1 + var.2)

which is hard to derive otherwise. 

they also using simulation and then the estimates will not match
perfectly.
